A fixed point can be a whole family

Toy Deutsch loop: the qubit that returns around the loop undergoes a Pauli-X flip. This is a quantum-state consistency calculation only; it does not model a spacetime path or send a signal.

ρC = ½(I + xX),   XρCX = ρC,   −1 ≤ x ≤ 1

Z-basis result: 50% / 50%
X-basis result (+ / −): 75% / 25%
State purity Tr(ρ²): 0.625

The classical bit rule sees only the Z-basis probabilities, so it selects 50/50. Quantum mechanics also tracks phase coherence: changing x changes X-basis statistics while leaving the state fixed under the flip. A loop rule therefore needs a fixed-point selection prescription if the outgoing state must be unique. Even then, a state rule is not the field's Green function, a 5D metric, or a route to an earlier event.
